title: Far Eastern Republic
capsule: The Far Eastern Republic (Дальневосточная Республика) was a nominally independent democratic buffer state established in April 1920 in Verkhneudinsk (modern Ulan-Ude), covering Transbaikal, Amur, Primorye, Sakhalin, and Kamchatka. Covertly directed by Moscow as a Soviet proxy, it served to avoid direct confrontation with Japan, which maintained occupation forces in Primorye; the republic maintained a coalition government, its own army (the People's Revolutionary Army), and diplomatic channels with Tokyo. After Japanese forces withdrew from Vladivostok in October 1922, the Far Eastern Republic's existence became unnecessary, and its assembly voted on 15 November 1922 to merge with the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic, abolishing the state.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The administrative boundaries of the Far Eastern Republic are reasonably well documented in Soviet and Japanese archival sources, though control over Sakhalin and parts of Primorye was contested and incomplete.
